diagnosis.micro: UAOS correctly diagnosed that Financial proactive-resolution was mostly rule/static-test evidence, then ended the audit by recommending a future executable bridge instead of executing the currently available governed repair.
diagnosis.macro: Problem detection, deliberation, recovery-before-user-escalation and observable-inheritance assurance were present, but there was no terminal admission rule requiring a detected repairable problem to move from cognition into current action.
diagnosis.assumption_challenged: A strong diagnosis plus a concrete recommendation is sufficient problem closure when the acting Agent already has authority and tools to repair the defect.

external_method_evidence: Kubernetes admission controllers make policy effective by intercepting an operation before persistence instead of relying on policy text alone.
Pact contract testing verifies executable interactions against a contract rather than treating the declaration itself as behavioral proof.

alternatives.failure_mode: Repeats the declaration-to-operation defect; the Agent can still stop at recommendation-only.
Overreaches authority, user-choice and safety boundaries and would make read-only diagnosis unsafe.
Still cannot claim host-level physical complete mediation, but it makes valid terminal states executable/testable and lets domains attach stronger receipts/probes.

candidate_changes: Add src/uaos/kernel/problem_closure.py with executable closure decisions and finalization admission.
Add SESSION_INTERACTION_POLICY 1.7 turn-level problem-to-action closure gate.
Promote COMMON_BEHAVIOR_ASSURANCE 1.2 with repair-or-block terminal semantics.
Bind registered-domain adoption to owner-native execution evidence rather than declaration-only claims.
Apply the new parent rule immediately to Financial via a separate child-owned candidate branch.
assurance_boundary: Executable policy and regression tests do not equal host-level physical interception of every natural-language response; physical complete mediation remains unclaimed.
